Based on what you’ve said (you already back up to an external drive, want more convenient central storage for laptop and phone, are a beginner, and are concerned about security), here’s a short decision guide:

- Buy now if: you’re running out of space or want the convenience of a central backup location immediately. A NAS will let you back up multiple devices centrally and avoid juggling external drives.
- Wait if: your current solution still meets your needs and you can spend a little time researching the right model (bays, security features, and ease of use) so you don’t overpay or buy more capacity than you need.

Key things to check when choosing now (or before you buy):
- Number of bays (2-bay vs 4-bay): pick based on how much storage and redundancy you want. 2-bay is cheaper and compact; 4-bay gives more capacity and RAID options.
- Security features: make sure the NAS supports encryption, granular access controls, and account protections (e.g., 2FA) since you said security matters.
- Ease of use and backup support: pick a beginner-friendly brand/model that makes backing up phones and laptops straightforward.
